backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, replace the constant INIT_RADIUS starting radii with a log-normal draw: r0 = INIT_RADIUS * exp(rng.normal(0, 0.5, n)), clipped to [0.005, 0.2]. This gives the first SLSQP run a spread of sizes instead of uniform circles, which may seed a more varied basin before basin hopping starts. Centres stay uniform in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Only the initial radii change.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed initial radii

backlog.spec: In basin-hopping solves, add to the SLSQP objective a small term 1e-3 * sum((v - x0)**2) over centres only, with its gradient, so the solve stays near the perturbed start and explores local basins; for the final 20 percent of time set the coefficient to 0. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Proximal anchor penalty in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, on half of the steps (chosen with rng) replace the independent Gaussian centre noise with a smooth low-frequency displacement field. Draw amplitudes A, B ~ N(0, 0.03), integer wave numbers kx, ky in {1, 2} and phases in [0, 2*pi) with rng. Set dx = A * sin(2*pi*ky*y + phase1) and dy = B * sin(2*pi*kx*x + phase2), computed from the incumbent centres, add them to the centres and clip to [0, 1]. Neighbouring circles then move together, rows and columns slide past each other, and the contact graph changes along a line instead of everywhere. On these steps add radius noise of sd 0.005 only. _relocate, SLSQP, _repair and acceptance run as before.
backlog.title: Smooth shear-field collective kick

backlog.spec: After each accepted incumbent, compute contacts (pairs with gap < 1e-6). Perturb with noise scaled per circle: sd 0.04 for circles with fewer than 3 contacts (rattlers or loose ones) and sd 0.01 for circles with 3 or more contacts. Everything else in the loop is unchanged.
backlog.title: Contact-graph-guided perturbation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the pair constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 with the squared form dx^2+dy^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0, and additionally require r_i+r_j >= 0 implicitly through the bounds already in place. The squared form removes the square-root singularity at zero distance, giving smoother gradients for SLSQP. Keep the same pair index arrays, the same wall constraints, and the same MAX_ITER. Only the cons function changes, so the rest of the basin-hopping loop stays identical.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints in SLSQP

backlog.spec: Maintain two packings: the incumbent and a second elite packing that is the best of all candidates whose radius sum is within 0.003 of the incumbent but differs from it in centre layout. Each basin-hopping step picks its parent at random from the two elites, with probability 0.5 each. Update the elites with each new candidate. This keeps a small population of distinct good basins instead of a single chain, and it uses only the existing moves, with no new solver code.
backlog.title: Keep an elite pair of packings and restart from the worse one

backlog.spec: After _repair produces a valid packing, add a pass that inflates each radius to its maximum feasible value given all other circles fixed. Loop over circles in order of increasing radius, and for each circle set r_i to min(wall distance, min over j of (d_ij - r_j)). Repeat the sweep twice. This recovers slack that the max-overlap repair leaves behind, and it is O(n^2) per sweep, which is cheap at n=32. Output must stay valid under the 1e-10 tolerance, so subtract a 1e-12 margin in the final radii.
backlog.title: Greedy radius inflation after repair

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP call in basin hopping, shrink the candidate radii so that the starting point is roughly feasible: multiply r0 by 0.9 and then cap each radius by its wall distance. SLSQP then starts from a nearly valid packing, which usually keeps the iterates on the feasible side and reduces the number of pair constraints it violates early. The shrink factor is the only new constant. Nothing else in the loop changes.
backlog.title: Feasibility-shrunk start before SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 before the SLSQP solve, pick one circle among the 5 smallest radii and one among the 5 largest, swap their centres (keeping radii attached to the circles, then shrink the swapped radii to fit, e.g. set both to the mean radius), then proceed with the existing perturbation, relocation and solve. Accept via the existing rule.
backlog.title: Swap small and large circle move

backlog.spec: Keep the search loop as it is, but reserve the last 10 percent of the TIME_FRACTION budget for one final polish of the best packing only. Run SLSQP on the incumbent centres and radii with ftol=1e-12 and maxiter=500, using the same constraints as _solve_once. Pass the result through _repair and keep it only if its radius sum beats the incumbent. This targets the small convergence gap left by the default SLSQP ftol of 1e-6 without spending time on the search itself.
backlog.title: Tight-tolerance final polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Add a topology move to the basin-hopping loop. With probability 0.15 per step (constant REFLECT_PROB), before the Gaussian noise, pick an axis a in {0, 1} and a side at random with rng. For every incumbent circle whose centre coordinate a lies on that side of 0.5, reflect that coordinate within the half: x -> 0.5 - x for the lower half, x -> 1.5 - x for the upper half. Radii are kept. Circles that straddle the midline may now overlap; the usual noise, _relocate, SLSQP and _repair deal with that. Acceptance is unchanged (the candidate must beat the incumbent). The aim is to recombine a good half-packing with a mirrored interface, a large coherent move that Gaussian noise cannot make.
backlog.title: Half-square reflection kick

backlog.spec: In _relocate, replace the 30 uniform random candidate points with the actual holes of the current packing. Compute scipy.spatial.Delaunay on the centres of all circles except k, plus the four square corners and four edge midpoints as extra points. Take the circumcentre of every triangle, keep those inside [0, 1]^2, and add 10 uniform random points as a fallback. For each candidate p compute rk = max(min(p.min(), (1 - p).min(), (d - r).min()), 0) with the k-th circle excluded, vectorised over candidates. Choose a candidate at random among the 3 with the largest rk, using rng, so that successive hops differ. Set c[k], r[k] to that point and its rk. Wrap the Delaunay call in try/except and fall back to the existing random-trial code on any error. The function signature stays the same.
backlog.title: Delaunay hole candidates for relocation

backlog.spec: Change _relocate to take a parameter m (default 1) and relocate the m smallest circles one after another. Each one is moved to the best of `trials` random points by the existing local score, and the score uses the radii already updated in that call. In the basin-hopping loop call it with m = 2 with probability 0.5, otherwise m = 1. No other changes.
backlog.title: Relocate the two smallest circles

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, replace the centre perturbation rng.normal(0, 0.02, bc.shape) with rng.normal(0, 1, bc.shape) * (0.4 * br[:, None] + 0.005), so that each circle's displacement scales with its radius (for a typical r ~0.09 this is about 0.04, for small circles about 0.01). Radius noise and relocation stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-proportional centre noise

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 per step, apply a random affine map about (0.5, 0.5) to the incumbent centres instead of the per-circle Gaussian noise: c0 = 0.5 + (bc - 0.5) @ (I + A).T, where A has i.i.d. N(0, 0.03) entries. Then clip to [0,1] and add N(0, 0.005) per-centre noise. Radii get the usual noise, and _relocate is still applied. This is a collective shear or stretch that can move many contacts at once.
backlog.title: Small random affine kick

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping step, scale the centre noise for each circle by its own radius: c0 = bc + rng.normal(0, sigma * (br / br.mean())[:, None], bc.shape), keeping sigma = 0.02. Large circles then move less and small circles move more, which matches the rattler-heavy structure of good packings. Radii noise stays the same. Clipping to [0, 1] and _relocate are unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-proportional perturbation noise

backlog.spec: In _relocate, the neighbour cutoff is currently the fixed value 0.05 added to rk + r. Replace it with a cutoff proportional to the typical circle size, nb = d < rk + r + 1.5 * np.mean(r). Circles with big radii then count as neighbours over a wider distance, so the relocation score reflects the local crowding more accurately. The scoring formula and the number of trials stay the same.
backlog.title: Scale-aware relocation neighbourhood

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed centre-noise sd of 0.02 in the basin-hopping step with a fresh value drawn each step: sigma = exp(rng.uniform(log(0.003), log(0.05))). Use this sigma for both the centre and the radius noise on that step. Spreading the step size over a log range gives the chain both fine local moves and coarse jumps without any schedule to tune. The relocation step and acceptance rule are unchanged.
backlog.title: Log-uniform random sigma per basin-hopping step

backlog.spec: After the basin-hopping loop, take the best centres and solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs): maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance of centre i, r_i >= 0, with centres fixed. Subtract SHRINK 1e-9 from the result, run the existing _repair for safety, and return it only if its sum beats the current best. Also apply this LP in place of _repair inside the loop for candidate evaluation.
backlog.title: Final LP polish of radii

memo: Helped: basin hopping replacing random restarts (slot 1, -2.9313/-2.9274) and relocating the smallest circle before each solve (slot 23, -2.9353/-2.9339; incumbent -2.9346 over 2 runs). Gains are close to the noise sd of 0.0034, so be cautious. Single unconfirmed runs 0.0019 or more better than the incumbent: slot 25 two-cluster merge start (-2.9366), slot 26 weighted objective (-2.9365), slot 30 two-stage wall tightening (-2.9368), slot 31 hard-disk Monte Carlo start (-2.9364). Did not help: longer time fraction (-2.9204), tied-radii start (-2.9225), penalty continuation (-2.9048), subset re-optimisation (-2.8822), symmetric start (-2.9155), pair-list pruning (-1.7220, broke the packing). Init changes, extra moves and heavy restructuring mostly failed or were neutral. Next: replicate slots 25, 26, 30 and 31, then stack the best one or two on the relocation move. Also try small in-loop tweaks such as swapping a small and a large circle. Keep edits small. The gap to the published 2.9370 is about 0.003.
